arc: A light-speed journey outward from Earth to the edge of the observable universe, one stop per episode. Each episode answers the previous cliffhanger, then teases the next stop.

episodes.title: Leaving Earth at Light Speed: Stop 1
episodes.topic: A light-speed journey outward from Earth, stop 1: the Moon (1.3 s away, drifting 3.8 cm/yr, laser mirrors, end of total eclipses)
episodes.hook: You just left Earth at the speed of light.
episodes.cliffhanger_question: After the Moon, what do you hit first: Venus, Mars, or the Sun?
episodes.summary: Premiere of the light-speed journey. Light circles Earth 7.5 times a second and reaches the Moon in 1.3 s; Apollo took 3 days. The Moon recedes 3.8 cm a year (measured with Apollo laser mirrors), so total solar eclipses end in ~600 million years.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 2: Venus Is Hell
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 2: Venus (closest at ~38 million km / ~2 light-minutes; 465°C; 92x pressure; spins backwards; day longer than year; Venera 13 survived 127 min)
episodes.hook: Venus wins. But only when it lines up perfectly.
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Could humans ever live on Mars? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: Answer: Venus is first when closest (~38 million km, ~2 light-minutes); Mars ~3 min, Sun 8 min 20 s. Venus: ~465°C (melts lead), pressure like 900 m underwater, spins backwards (Sun rises in the west), day longer than its year, Soviet Venera 13 lasted ~2 hours in 1982. Next stop: Mars.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 3: Could We Live on Mars?
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 3: Mars (~3 light-minutes when closest; air <1% of Earth's; ~-60°C; Olympus Mons ~2.5x Everest; blue sunsets; planet-wide dust storms; Phobos spiralling inward)
episodes.hook: Without a suit, Mars knocks you out in seconds.
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Is the asteroid belt packed with rocks like in the movies? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: Answer: not without sealed, shielded habitats. Mars: ~3 light-minutes when closest, air under 1% of Earth's, ~-60°C average, Olympus Mons ~2.5x Everest, blue sunsets, planet-wide dust storms, Phobos spiralling inward (crash or ring in tens of millions of years). Next stop: the asteroid belt.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 4: The Asteroid Belt Lie
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 4: the asteroid belt (~10 light-minutes to inner edge at closest; asteroids ~1 million km apart on average; total mass ~3% of the Moon; Ceres ~1/3 of that; salt deposits in Occator crater; Jupiter's gravity prevented a planet)
episodes.hook: The movies lied to you about asteroid belts.
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Is Jupiter Earth's protector or its biggest threat?
episodes.summary: Answer: no, the belt is almost empty. ~10 light-minutes from Earth to its inner edge at closest, asteroids ~1 million km apart on average, every spacecraft crossed safely. Total mass ~3% of the Moon, about a third of it in dwarf planet Ceres (bright salt deposits). Scientists think Jupiter's gravity stopped a planet forming. Next stop: Jupiter.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 5: Jupiter, Hero or Threat?
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 5: Jupiter (~35 light-minutes at closest; ~1,300 Earths fit inside; over twice the mass of all other planets combined; deflects and redirects comets; Shoemaker-Levy 9 in 1994; Great Red Spot wider than Earth; day under 10 hours)
episodes.hook: Jupiter is your bodyguard and your biggest threat.
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Will Saturn's rings vanish one day? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: Answer: both. Jupiter throws some comets away and flings others toward us. ~35 light-minutes at closest, ~1,300 Earths fit inside, more than twice the mass of all other planets combined. Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 hit it in 1994, leaving scars bigger than Earth. Great Red Spot is wider than Earth; a day lasts under 10 hours. Next stop: Saturn.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 6: Saturn's Dying Rings
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 6: Saturn (~67 light-minutes at closest; rings about 280,000 km wide but mostly only ~10 m thick; mostly water ice; ring rain drains them; may vanish in ~100-300 million years; less dense than water; Titan and Enceladus)
episodes.hook: Saturn's rings are disappearing right now.
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Does it rain diamonds on Uranus and Neptune? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: Answer: yes, the rings will vanish. ~67 light-minutes at closest. Rings span ~280,000 km but are mostly only ~10 m thick, mostly water ice. Ring material rains into Saturn; scientists think they could be gone in 100-300 million years. Saturn is less dense than water. Next stop: Uranus and Neptune.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 7: Diamond Rain on Ice Giants?
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 7: Uranus and Neptune (Uranus ~2.4 light-hours at closest, Neptune ~4 light-hours; scientists think diamond rain deep inside; Uranus tilted ~98 degrees; Neptune winds ~2,000 km/h; only Voyager 2 visited, in 1986 and 1989)
episodes.hook: Scientists think it rains diamonds out here.
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Is a ninth planet hiding beyond Neptune? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: Answer: probably yes, deep inside. Scientists think extreme pressure turns carbon into diamonds that sink. Uranus ~2.4 light-hours away, tipped ~98 degrees; Neptune ~4 light-hours, winds ~2,000 km/h. Only Voyager 2 ever visited. Next stop: beyond Neptune, a possible ninth planet.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 8: Is Planet Nine Real?
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 8: the Kuiper Belt and Pluto (~5.5 light-hours; Pluto demoted 2006; New Horizons 2015; hypothesized Planet Nine ~5-10 Earth masses, orbit ~10,000-20,000 years, never observed)
episodes.hook: Is a ninth planet hiding out here?
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Has anything humans built actually left the solar system? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: Answer: maybe. Scientists think odd orbits of distant icy worlds hint at an unseen planet 5 to 10 times Earth's mass, but nobody has ever seen it. Pluto sits ~5.5 light-hours away, demoted in 2006 and visited by New Horizons in 2015. Next stop: interstellar space.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 9: Voyager 1 Escaped
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 9: interstellar space and Voyager 1 (left heliosphere 2012; launched 1977; ~1 light-day away; ~17 km/s; golden record; Proxima Centauri ~4.2 light-years, Proxima b in habitable zone)
episodes.hook: Yes. One machine has already escaped.
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Could the planet at our nearest star hold life? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: Answer: yes, Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012. Launched in 1977, it is about one light-day away, moving ~17 km/s, and still talks to Earth. Even so, the nearest star is about 70,000 years away at that speed. Next stop: Proxima Centauri.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 10: Proxima b, Life?
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 10: Proxima Centauri b (4.2 light-years; ~11-day year; habitable zone; red dwarf flares; probably tidally locked; atmosphere unknown)
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Are there more planets than stars in our galaxy? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: Answer: maybe. Proxima b orbits in its star's habitable zone, 4.2 light-years away, but flares and tidal locking may strip its air. We still don't know if it has an atmosphere. Next stop: the Milky Way.

episodes.title: Light Speed Stop 11: The Milky Way
episodes.topic: Light-speed journey stop 11: the Milky Way (~100,000 light-years across; ~100-400 billion stars; most stars have planets; Sun ~26,000 light-years from center; orbit ~230 million years; Sagittarius A* ~4 million Suns)
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Is the Milky Way on a collision course with another galaxy? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: Answer: yes, astronomers estimate most stars have at least one planet. The Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across with hundreds of billions of stars and a black hole at its heart. Next stop: our neighbor Andromeda.

episodes.title: NASA Found Mars Rocks That Can Trap Fossils
episodes.topic: News: Perseverance finds large hydrated-silica rocks at 'Idubi' in Jezero crater (NASA update Nov 16, 2026). On Earth, silica preserves microfossils for billions of years. No life found.
episodes.hook: NASA found Mars rocks that can trap fossils.
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Do you think Mars ever had life? Yes or no?
episodes.summary: News reel: Perseverance found pale rocks at 'Idubi' rich in hydrated silica, which forms with water and on Earth preserves microfossils for billions of years. Earlier finds were too small to study; these are big enough. No life found yet.

episodes.title: Ek Tukda, Pahaad Jitna Bhaari: Neutron Star
episodes.topic: Evergreen: neutron stars. Sugar-cube-sized piece weighs about a billion tons (NASA's 'a mountain' comparison); more mass than the Sun in a ~20 km ball; born when a giant star's core collapses in a supernova; some spin over 700 times a second.
episodes.hook: Chini ka cube, pahaad jitna bhaari!
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Ise paas se dekhoge? Haan ya naa?
episodes.summary: Hinglish evergreen reel: a sugar-cube-sized piece of a neutron star weighs about as much as a mountain. Formed when a giant star's core collapses; more mass than the Sun packed into about 20 km; some spin over 700 times a second; gravity near it would flatten you.

episodes.title: Voyager 1 Ab Ek Light-Day Door Hai
episodes.topic: News: Voyager 1 reached one light-day (~25.9 billion km) from Earth on Nov 18, 2026 (NASA). First human-made object to do so; a radio message takes a full day each way; Voyager 2 reaches the mark around 2035.
episodes.hook: Voyager 1 ab ek light-day door hai!
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Kya yeh kabhi kisi star tak pahunchegi? Haan ya naa?
episodes.summary: News reel: on Nov 18, 2026 Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth (~25.9 billion km). Signals take a day each way. Voyager 2 reaches the mark around 2035.

episodes.title: Subah Dekho: Venus Sabse Zyada Chamak Raha Hai
episodes.topic: Event: Venus reaches greatest brilliancy in the morning sky around Nov 27-29, 2026. Look east/east-southeast 1-2 hours before dawn; no telescope needed. Venus's brightness comes from its reflective sulfuric-acid clouds.
episodes.hook: Is hafte Venus sabse zyada chamakta hai!
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Tumne kabhi Venus ko subah dekha hai? Haan ya naa?
episodes.summary: Event reel: Venus peaks in brightness in the morning sky around Nov 27-29, 2026. Look east, 1-2 hours before sunrise, no telescope needed. Its glow comes from highly reflective clouds hiding a ~465C surface; people often mistake it for a UFO.

episodes.title: Sunday Ko Space Station Ke Liye Cargo Launch
episodes.topic: Event: Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Cygnus XL cargo launch on a Falcon 9 targeted Sunday Nov 29, 2026 ~10:47 a.m. EST from Cape Canaveral; ~11,000 lb cargo incl. science experiments; ISS capture by Canadarm2 Dec 1; stays until May 2027.
episodes.hook: Astronauts ke liye Sunday ko cargo launch hoga!
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Live launch dekhna chahoge? Haan ya naa?
episodes.summary: Event reel: Cygnus XL cargo ship launches on Falcon 9 on Nov 29, 2026 (target, may slip), carrying about 11,000 lb (~5,000 kg) of supplies and experiments; Canadarm2 captures it Dec 1; stays at the ISS until May 2027.

episodes.title: Agar Sooraj Black Hole Ban Jaaye Toh?
episodes.topic: Evergreen: what if the Sun turned into a black hole of the same mass: Earth keeps orbiting; darkness and gravity change arrive after ~8 minutes (speed of light); we would freeze; the Sun is too light to become a black hole naturally.
episodes.hook: Sooraj black hole ban jaaye toh kya hoga?
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Andhera ya thand? Tumhe kya zyada darr lagega?
episodes.summary: Evergreen: if the Sun became a black hole of the same mass, nothing changes for 8 minutes, then the sky goes dark but Earth keeps orbiting because gravity stays the same; we would freeze. The Sun is too light to ever become a black hole.

episodes.title: NASA Ka Maara Asteroid Pehli Baar Dikha
episodes.topic: News: ESA's Hera released detailed images of Didymos and Dimorphos (~Nov 25-26, 2026): a stadium-sized crater/flattened side on Dimorphos from NASA's 2022 DART impact, hundreds of boulders orbiting, asteroid tumbling; Hera ~25-30 km away, approaching to ~13 km next month.
episodes.hook: NASA ka maara asteroid dikh gaya!
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Asteroid aaye toh tum kya chunoge: takkar ya bhaagna?
episodes.summary: News reel: ESA's Hera probe sent new close-ups of the asteroid NASA hit in 2022. Dimorphos has a stadium-sized crater, hundreds of boulders orbit the pair, and it still tumbles. Hera moves in to about 13 km next month.

episodes.title: Moon Ke Footprints Kab Tak Rahenge?
episodes.topic: Evergreen: Apollo footprints on the Moon survive because there is no wind or rain; only micrometeorites slowly erode them (~1 mm per million years); estimates say millions of years or more.
episodes.hook: Moon ke footprints lakhon saal nahi mitenge!
episodes.cliffhanger_question: Moon par tum kya chhodoge: footprint ya naam?
episodes.summary: Evergreen reel: Apollo bootprints on the Moon last because there is no wind or rain; tiny space dust wears them down by about a millimetre per million years, so they likely last millions of years.
